newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Pequots open $400 mln hotel, casino.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Pequots open $400 mln hotel, casino.

text.p: The Mashantucket Pequot Indian tribe said Thursday it opened the first phase of a hotel and conference center at their Foxwoods Resort Casino, which will cost more than $350 million when finished in 1998.
The 400-member Pequot tribe opened Foxwoods in 1992, and it has grown into the largest casino in the world, with estimated annual revenues of more than $1 billion.
The new Pequot Tower Casino adds 50,000 square feet of gaming space, set in a posh hotel and conference center that is scheduled to grow in phases through spring of 1998.
The lower levels of the 17-storey hotel opened on Thursday, along with two restaurants.
The 812 guest rooms are scheduled to be opened in phases over the next nine months, the Pequots said.
With the addition of Pequot Towers, the Foxwoods resort will have more than 1,400 rooms in three hotels.
The Pequots and the Mohegan Indians, who operate the competing Mohegan Sun casino about 10 miles away, give the state of Connecticut 25 percent of their slot machine revenues.
For the current fiscal year, the state's take from the slots is projected at $247.3 million, the Hartford Courant reported on Thursday.
This is the state's fourth-largest source of revenue behind the income tax, the sales tax and the corporation tax.
